text:
jamie: quick handoff — I'm off in ~20. Current state: embedding ingestion in eu-west1 is queued (~1.2k msgs) and we're seeing intermittent storage 429s. Also saw a dedupe-worker CPU thrash that impacted background throughput.

chen: noticed the spike, scaled embed-ingest from 3->6 replicas (`kubectl scale deploy embed-ingest --replicas=6 -n inference`). KV cache hit-rate dropped during the burst; bumped redis client pool and increased cache TTL to 60s.

sarah: rolled back canary for v2-encoder at 03:12 UTC. Enabled fallback route to `small-encoder-quant` for low-priority jobs so frontend latency stays steady. CPU on the dedupe worker is trending down.

ops-bot: INCIDENT created: #INC-2026-409 embed-ingest-euw1-queueing — runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/embed-ingest

chen: blocker — s3 multipart uploads returning 429 on small objects (~5–50KB). I'm increasing retries/backoff locally (`s3.max_retries 8->12`, `retry_backoff 250ms->500ms`) and re-ingesting a sample set to validate. If this continues we should route uploads to us-west as a temporary mitigation.

jamie: next steps — chen to open cloud support ticket + post upload traces in the incident thread. sarah to run `scripts/purge_stale_queues --age 2h --region eu-west1` at 02:00 UTC and share results. I'll keep canary disabled until encoder perf is validated for 24h.

oncall-next: taking over. I'll set an alert for queue > 500 and watch the embed SLOs. If queue persists > 1k for 30m I will flip to the reduced-priority routing policy. ping me directly for immediate rollbacks.

jamie: pasted a log snippet into the incident channel: ```WARN embed-ingest: dropped request: http 503, queue_size=1273, worker=ingest-4```

sarah: draft postmortem template started, adding traces and flame graphs now. Will attach CPU flamegraph + encoder timeline. @chen please add the storage traces.

chen: ack — uploaded traces to the incident thread and included a temporary config diff. Diff highlights: `s3.max_retries=12`, `retry_backoff_ms=500`, `multipart_chunk=5MB -> 8MB`.

jamie: wrapping up — no open pages tied to external alerts, rolling metrics look stable after scaling and rollback. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
